title: Career Roadmap: Merchandiser
summary: An Apparel Merchandiser acts as a link between buyers, designers, suppliers, production teams and quality-control departments. The role helps ensure that garments are developed according to the buyer's specifications, produced within the agreed budget and delivered on schedule.

about.label: Core Focus
about.text: Product planning, sample development, costing, production coordination, quality tracking and delivery management

about.label: Work Settings
about.text: Garment factories, apparel exporters, fashion brands, buying houses, textile companies and retail sourcing firms

about.label: Suitable For
about.text: Students interested in fashion, garment production, business coordination, product costing and supply chains

blocks.text: An Apparel Merchandiser acts as a link between buyers, designers, suppliers, production teams and quality-control departments. The role helps ensure that garments are developed according to the buyer's specifications, produced within the agreed budget and delivered on schedule.
Responsibilities often include interpreting buyer requirements, coordinating samples, preparing cost sheets, tracking materials, monitoring production progress and communicating delivery updates.
This roadmap focuses on fashion and apparel merchandising, rather than retail store merchandising alone.

blocks.text: Progression depends on technical garment knowledge, costing accuracy, communication, buyer coordination and the ability to manage production timelines.

sections.heading: Step-by-Step Roadmap During the B.Voc Degree

blocks.text: The following plan can be adapted to a three-year programme.

blocks.label: Year 1
blocks.text: Fashion, Textiles and Garment Fundamentals

blocks.label: Goal
blocks.text: Understand how garments are designed, constructed and manufactured.

rows.text: Natural and synthetic fibres, yarns, fabric construction and finishes
Woven, knitted and nonwoven fabrics; weight, width and shrinkage
Seams, stitches, components, trims and construction methods
Silhouettes, garment categories, colour and trend awareness
Measurements, size charts, fit and grading fundamentals
Cutting, sewing, finishing, pressing and packing
Defects, measurement tolerances and inspection basics
Emails, reports, meeting notes and professional coordination

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Identify common fabric types and record their properties.
Create a garment specification sheet for a basic T-shirt or shirt.
Prepare a measurement chart for a simple garment.
Document the manufacturing steps for a sample apparel product.
Create a glossary of garment construction terms.
Compare the construction and material choices of two similar garments.

blocks.label: Year 1 outcome
blocks.text: The student can understand garment components, fabrics, measurements and the basic apparel production process.

blocks.label: Year 2
blocks.text: Merchandising, Costing and Sampling

blocks.label: Goal
blocks.text: Learn to convert buyer requirements into a production-ready garment order.

rows.text: Interpret product briefs, specifications and delivery requirements
Read measurement charts, sketches, construction details and bill of materials
Coordinate proto samples, fit samples, size sets and pre-production samples
Calculate fabric, trims, labour, overheads and other cost components
Understand garment consumption, marker efficiency and wastage
Follow up on fabric, trims, labels and packaging materials
Understand order quantities, production capacity and lead times
Identify defects and follow inspection and corrective-action procedures
Maintain order sheets, sample comments, approvals and status trackers

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Prepare a sample tech pack for a shirt, T-shirt or pair of trousers.
Create a garment costing sheet using sample material and labour rates.
Develop a sample approval tracker.
Prepare a fabric and trims requirement sheet for a small order.
Simulate a buyer revision and document the changes required.
Create a production timeline covering sampling, material sourcing, manufacturing and shipment.

blocks.label: Year 2 outcome
blocks.text: The student can prepare basic merchandising documents, estimate product costs and coordinate sample and material workflows.

blocks.label: Year 3
blocks.text: Production Coordination and Industry Readiness

blocks.label: Goal
blocks.text: Manage the progress of an apparel order from development to shipment under appropriate supervision.

rows.text: Track order requirements, quantities, specifications and deadlines
Monitor fabric, trims and packaging availability
Compare planned and actual production progress
Track defects, inspection results and corrective actions
Identify changes affecting material use, labour and margins
Understand common shipping and order documents where relevant
Prepare accurate progress reports and professional updates
Seek experience with an apparel manufacturer, exporter, sourcing firm or fashion brand

blocks.text: Recommended final-year projects

items.text: Develop a complete merchandising file for a hypothetical garment order.
Prepare a tech pack and costing sheet for a T-shirt or shirt.
Build an order-tracking dashboard using Excel.
Compare fabric consumption and estimated cost for two garment designs.
Create a sample approval and revision management system.
Develop a production timeline and identify potential bottlenecks.
Prepare a quality inspection report with defect categories and corrective actions.
Create a sourcing proposal comparing fabric or trim suppliers using sample data.

blocks.label: Year 3 outcome
blocks.text: The student can demonstrate a structured apparel merchandising workflow, accurate documentation and basic production coordination.

rows.text: Communicates the buyer's garment requirements to the production team

blocks.text: Essential costing calculations

blocks.label: Material cost
blocks.text: Required material quantity × material rate.

blocks.label: Cost per garment
blocks.text: Total order cost ÷ planned order quantity, when the cost calculation uses the full order.

blocks.label: Material wastage allowance
blocks.text: Additional material quantity included according to the relevant process and product assumptions.

blocks.label: Example
blocks.text: If a sample garment requires 1.5 metres of fabric at ₹120 per metre, the basic fabric cost is ₹180 per garment before wastage, trims, labour and other expenses.
Actual costing methods vary by product, factory, order terms and sourcing arrangement.

blocks.text: For this B.Voc pathway, prioritize garment and textile knowledge + costing + tech-pack documentation + Excel + sample and production coordination.

Students who enjoy communication and coordination can focus on buyer-facing merchandising. Those who prefer numbers can specialize in costing and sourcing, while students who enjoy factory processes can move toward production planning and quality coordination.

The most valuable graduation outcome is a portfolio demonstrating how a garment order moves from buyer brief → product specification → sampling → costing → production tracking → quality checks → delivery. This helps employers assess whether the student understands the practical workflow of apparel merchandising.
